public_rationale: The claim describes conditions in 2024, up to the post date of 1 January 2025. On 7 November 2024, OpenAI researchers wrote that current frontier models sometimes produce false outputs, known as hallucinations. They also called training models to give factually correct answers an open problem (e1). The same paper introduced SimpleQA, a set of short fact-seeking questions, and said GPT-4o and Claude both scored under 50% on it (e2). None of the cited evidence shows a method that reliably removed hallucinations across varied tasks by the end of 2024. Under the contract, a lab saying in late 2024 that hallucination was unsolved counts as support, so the claim holds on a plain reading.
limitations: The main source is a lab paper describing its own models' limits. Independent leaderboard figures for late 2024 could not be read.
A SimpleQA score under 50% is not the same as a hallucination rate, because the benchmark also counts questions the model did not attempt.
The evidence does not measure hallucination rates in grounded settings such as retrieval or summarization.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: There is still no robust solution to LLM hallucinations.

statement.excerpt: There is still no robust solution to hallucinations.
statement.document_title: 25 AI Predictions for 2025, from Marcus on AI

our_interpretation: Plain reading: as of the end of 2024, no available method reliably stopped LLMs from producing confident false statements across ordinary tasks.
He states a current condition without a period. Since the post reviews 2024, the target period is calendar 2024 up to the post date.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence from late 2024 shows leading LLMs still hallucinate at meaningful rates, or that leading labs still treat hallucination as unsolved.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence shows a method or model that, by the end of 2024, reliably removed hallucinations across varied tasks in independent tests.
